## Design

### 2026-10-28: This session I designed the whole PCB for my alarm clock.

**4.5h**

This session I designed the whole PCB for my alarm clock.
To start, I had to do some research on what components I should use. I settled on an ESP32 devkit 32E to control it, a dfplayer mini to play the alarm, and the TM1637 for the display.

Some of this was tricky because I had to go looking for the symbols and footprints for these components which took a bit of time. I also had to do some research to figure out exactly how to wire the components, and I am relatively confident that I got it right.

Like last time, when I was about halfway through with the PCB my Kicad instance crashed causing me to loose a lot of progress. This is an issue I will need to fix in the future. On this board I also have compnents placed on different sides to that the casing and button pressing won't interfere with the components.

After finishing all of the schematic and trace routing, a had a bit too much fun placing designs and images around the board. This is by far the most personalized board I've made yet, and I'm really happy with how it turned out!

After this, I exported all of the files and uploaded them to the project github.

### 2026-10-29: In this session I did the 3d modeling for the enclosure of the alarm clock.

**4h**

In this session I did the 3d modeling for the enclosure of the alarm clock.

First I designed the body of it. I has a lip on the inside to support the PCB and a cavity below to hold the electronics. There is also a hole in the front for the screen and the back for the speaker and USBC port. When I finished this, I realized that the button wasn't centered  on the PCB, so instead of redesigning the PCB, I changed the geometry of the body so that it would fall in the canter anyway.

It was around this time that I learned bout keyboard stabilizers, so I spent a while researching them, and ended up deciding it probably won't be necessary for my build because of the use case.

After this I designed the lid for it. I was trying to use the loft feature, but it wasn't cooperating. However, I eventually was able to finish it it and I'm pretty happy with how t turned out! The lid is designed to be a press fit on the body.

Overall, I'm definitely getting better and faster at 3d modeling, but I still have a long way to go! Now all I need to do is create to code for the clock itself and make the shortcut to control it from my phone.
